title: Tier-aware alert routing for SLO burn-rate alerts (Hosted -> platform-oncall, Dedicated -> dedicated-oncall)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Internal only: burn-rate alerts now route to the correct oncall rotation by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated).
body:
Summary: This PR makes SLO burn-rate alert routing tier-aware. Dedicated tier alerts page dedicated-oncall; Hosted tier alerts page platform-oncall. It also adds an end-to-end contract test that validates the Alertmanager -> alert-router -> PagerDuty/Slack payloads for both tiers.

Motivation: As we roll out tiered SLOs + error budgets, burn-rate alerts are currently hitting the same paging target, which has (1) created confusion during Dedicated customer events and (2) pulled platform-oncall into Dedicated-specific capacity/readiness investigations unnecessarily. We want alert routing to align with ownership while keeping a safe fallback route when tier is missing.

What changed: (1) Alert routing rules: Introduced a tier-based routing decision in alert-router using alert labels `tier` (hosted|dedicated) and `slo_scope` (api|embeddings|catalog|pool_readiness). Dedicated routes to PagerDuty service `dedicated-oncall` and Slack `#dedicated-oncall`; Hosted routes to PagerDuty service `platform-oncall` and Slack `#eng-oncall`. (2) Guardrails: If `tier` is missing/unknown, we default to platform-oncall and attach an annotation `routing_fallback=platform-oncall` to make mislabeling visible; we also emit a counter `alert_router_fallback_total{reason="missing_tier"}` to help detect instrumentation gaps. (3) Payload normalization: Standardized alert annotations to ensure `runbook_url`, `dashboard_url`, and `error_budget_policy_url` are always present for burn-rate alerts, even when upstream rules omit optional fields. (4) End-to-end tests: Added a staging-mode integration test that posts representative Alertmanager payloads (Hosted burn spike; Dedicated pool readiness burn spike) to the alert-router HTTP endpoint and asserts the resulting PagerDuty Events v2 payload fields (routing key selection, dedup key, severity, and custom details). This is designed to prevent silent regressions when we edit labels/annotations in Prometheus rules.

Testing: Unit tests cover routing decisions and fallback behavior. Integration test runs in CI with stubbed PagerDuty client and a golden payload comparison. Manual staging test run documented in the PR comments.

Rollout plan: Deploy alert-router change behind `ALERT_ROUTING_TIER_AWARE=true` in staging for 24h; then enable in prod. No changes are required to customer-facing dashboards. Note: This does not change paging thresholds; it only changes who gets paged.

Notes/Dependencies: Relies on tier label propagation landing for burn-rate alerts (see prior work on tier dimension propagation). If any burn-rate alert rules still lack `tier`, they will continue to page platform-oncall, with a visible annotation + metric to drive cleanup.
commits: alert-router: route burn-rate alerts based on `tier` label
alert-router: add fallback metric + annotation for missing/unknown tier
observability: normalize runbook/dashboard/policy annotations for burn alerts
tests: add Alertmanager->PagerDuty e2e payload contract test fixtures
chore: update oncall docs references for tier-aware routing
conversation:
Allison Grant (reviewer): Can we confirm the fallback behavior is safe? I don't want Dedicated to ever route to platform-oncall just because of a typo in tier.
Sergio Costa (author): Yep. Unknown/missing tier falls back to platform-oncall intentionally (safer default since platform-oncall is staffed 24/7 and can triage). To make typos obvious, I added `routing_fallback=platform-oncall` annotation + `alert_router_fallback_total{reason="unknown_tier"}` metric. For Dedicated rules we also added a unit test verifying tier is strictly `dedicated` or it will not match the dedicated route.

Rafael Mendes (reviewer): For Dedicated, should we page dedicated-oncall for *all* burn-rate alerts? Some are low-sev and should be ticket-only.
Sergio Costa (author): This PR only changes routing targets, not severity/thresholds. The paging-vs-ticket policy stays in Prometheus rules (and the policy doc). That said, Dedicated currently has two alert classes: page (multi-window fast burn) and ticket (slow burn). Both will now notify dedicated-oncall channels appropriately; we can adjust thresholds in ENG-2420 follow-ups if noise is high.

Connor O'Brien (reviewer): Please add an explicit test that we preserve dedup keys across both tiers. We had incident spam last quarter due to dedup drift.
Sergio Costa (author): Added. Contract test now asserts `dedup_key = ${alertname}:${service}:${region}:${tier}` and we keep it stable for both hosted/dedicated fixtures.

Amara Diallo (reviewer): Minor: the annotation normalizer should not override runbook_url if it’s already present upstream.
Sergio Costa (author): Good catch. Updated to only backfill missing fields, never overwrite.

Allison Grant (reviewer): Approved after the fallback metric + dedup assertions. Please link the error budget policy URL in the PD custom details.
Sergio Costa (author): Done in `pagerduty_events.ts` (custom_details.error_budget_policy_url).
